comments.text:
the matter of fact is that CoPilot lies about what it outputs. It often outputs plain wrong code (that is full of errors, often you can even find the snippets on github from which it copied and pasted components without understanding what it's doing) and then, when in the chat window is asked about what the error is it made, it will pretend that it never created any code or not that code or that the code it just presented one answer above is not from CoPilot. 
Working with CoPilot has dramatically slowed my development down, as I have to constantly fight an Artificial Idiot that keeps writing wrong code, lies about what it did and does not even understand what the difference between "unsigned integer" and "float" is (I am frequently running into that: Provide a result from this function in unsigned integer" will often create a "float(result)" type of function.

CoPilot is INCREDIBLY dumb. Yes, it can help with setting up basic frameworks - but any seasoned developer already HAS a vast library of basic frameworks, so CoPilot is just a "search engine" for that. 
Any actual DEVELOPMENT where even the faintest understanding of what the code is supposed to do is required will get dramatically slowed down - compared to experienced code writing - instead of spead up.

Again, the product does have its advantages, but is highly overprized. You get the same quality of results from free LLMs that you run locally as a server. You don't need internet to do that, it's often faster and not worse in quality. If you want more sophisticated responses, you have to check out other vendors' products (not naming the elephant in the room here), but CoPilot is definitely not even in the top ten.
